parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the core requirements: pure ESM .mjs files in /output, local imports, manual process.argv parsing, byte builder behavior, Python bytes repr formatting, and sample parity with the executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It used a four-child swarm: pybytes, construct, argparse, and entrypoint/integration. The parent retained final verification ownership after all child handoffs returned.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote /output/lib/pybytes.mjs, /output/lib/construct.mjs, /output/lib/argparse.mjs, and /output/test17.mjs. The argparse child implemented the narrowed regex/safe-integer contract it was given.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The entry child waited for the libraries, inspected the interfaces, wrote the entrypoint, and the parent later read the generated files and delivered the four-file tree.
parallel.verification: The run used sample probes, child self-tests, entrypoint tests, a local differential shell harness for samples, boundary cases, random valid cases, and selected error cases, plus a grep/file-list check.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 1 of 30 cases. The mounted inputs do not reveal the testcase; the visible parallel-specific final gap is weaker argparse parity from the child brief.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same prompt requirements and progressively expanded them with executable probes for bytes repr, argparse help/errors, option ordering, duplicate arguments, Unicode digits, underscores, and edge cases.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned discovery, module design, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery, with no delegation or subagent handoff.
serial.implementation: It wrote python-int, python-repr, construct, argument-parser, and test17 modules, including BigInt-style integer handling and broader Python argparse emulation than the parallel argparse module.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It assembled all local modules into /output/test17.mjs, corrected the help-option edge case, checked the file tree, and presented the final code layout.
serial.verification: It ran the sample cases, parser failure comparisons, syntax checks, 500 randomized black-box cases with stdout/stderr/status comparison, and supplemental Unicode/whitespace integer parsing comparisons.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 1 of 30 cases despite broader local verification; the mounted summaries do not identify the failing testcase.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the main ESM, /output, byte-building, manual argparse, and output-repr requirements, but delegated argparse with a simplified integer-parsing assumption.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same top-level task and also probed edge CLI behavior such as underscores, Unicode digits, help text, and option error ordering.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both covered the main task, but serial developed a richer model of Python argparse while parallel narrowed that requirement at delegation time.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent split ownership by file across four child agents and retained final verification responsibility.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor kept implementation, integration, and verification ownership in one continuous control flow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used component ownership with parent integration checks; serial avoided handoffs and evolved the design in a single actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel established explicit module interfaces, but the argparse child brief converted exact Python parsing into a narrower regex and safe-integer contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept discoveries in one context and carried edge-case findings forward into the implemented parser and supplemental verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The interface contract worked across files, but one child task lost task-requirement breadth; serial had no transfer boundary for that knowledge.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a smaller four-file implementation with Buffer-based builders, bytes repr, a simple argparse module, and a test17 entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a five-file implementation, separating Python integer parsing and repr formatting, then integrating them into the entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced working modular ports for common cases; serial invested more implementation in CLI-parity edge cases while parallel kept the delegated argparse module simpler.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four child results returned through AgentSwarm, then the parent ran verification and read final files before responding.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results; local file edits, probes, and verification remained in one actor through final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had completed child handoffs and no trapped result; serial had no result lifecycle boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children wrote separate files in the same /output tree, but the parent later listed and read the final files and no collision or overwrite is visible.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote and edited files itself, listed the final tree, and kept provenance in one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used shared workspace writes with file-level separation; serial used one-writer control. No concrete write collision is evidenced.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent ran a shell differential harness over samples, boundary cases, random valid cases, and selected error cases, but compared only stdout and exit status in that parent harness.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran focused parser comparisons, syntax checks, a 500-case black-box comparison of stdout, stderr, and status, and supplemental numeric parsing checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verification was broader and included stderr and Python integer parsing edges; parallel verification was sufficient for many cases but narrower.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished quickly with four subagents, no timeout, and local verification before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial took longer but also finished without timeout, using the extra time for deeper probing and randomized checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no budget exhaustion in either run; the main difference is that serial spent more elapsed time on deep verification while parallel used fan-out for fast construction.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both modes have current completed official evaluations with solution_passed false and 29 of 30 samples passed, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The concrete task-solving difference is process and implementation depth: the parallel run decomposed by module and accepted a simplified argparse child result, while the serial run kept all knowledge local, probed more CLI edge cases, and implemented richer Python-integer parsing. The common 29/30 result cannot be reduced to a parallel coordination root cause from the mounted inputs because no failing testcase details are available.
parallel_contributors: Parallel fan-out produced the required file tree quickly and integrated all child results.
The argparse child brief narrowed exact Python CLI parity into ASCII digit and safe-integer parsing, leaving a final parser gap relative to the prompt.
serial_contributors: Serial probing discovered broader argparse behavior and fed it directly into the single-actor implementation.
Serial verification covered stdout, stderr, exit status, Unicode integer parsing, and supplemental parser cases.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs still failed one official sample; the mounted summaries do not reveal whether this was stderr, an untested edge case, or evaluator-specific behavior.
The common failure is not explained by child cancellation, missing join, write collision, or timeout.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official metrics are mounted, so the individual failing testcase is unavailable for direct attribution.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
